balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Lendlease Group: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Lendlease Group: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

distributions.title: Distributions
distributions.content:
Cash distributed per share or unit.

For Lendlease Group: a policy of paying a fixed percentage of NAV keeps NAV flat by design.

What to watch:

  • Distribution policy versus earnings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Lendlease Group: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Lendlease Group: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fum.title: Assets and funds under management
fum.content:
Funds under management (FUM) is the capital invested in Lendlease's managed real-estate funds and mandates; assets under management (AUM) is the broader figure including co-investments and assets managed but not in a dedicated fund. The Investments segment's fee income scales with FUM, not with group revenue.

For Lendlease Group: Investments is management's targeted ~50% of long-run EBITDA mix, built on compounding FUM; a shrinking FUM base (management flagged a further FY26 decline from portfolio recycling, not yet in this series) works against that target.

What to watch:

  • FUM growing or shrinking relative to prior periods
  • The gap between AUM and FUM (co-investment and non-fund mandates)
  • Whether fee income (in the Growth & Profitability charts) tracks FUM

constructionPipeline.title: Construction backlog and new work secured
constructionPipeline.content:
New work secured is construction contracts won in the period; backlog revenue is the unrecognised contract value still to be delivered. Backlog next period roughly equals this period's backlog plus new work secured, less revenue recognised as projects complete -- so new work secured below revenue recognised means the backlog, and future Construction revenue, is shrinking.

For Lendlease Group: Construction is Australia-only fee/fixed-price delivery for government and corporate clients; FY2026 backlog rose 42% to $8.4bn on $6.4bn of new work secured, the basis for management's guided revenue growth into FY2027-28.

What to watch:

  • New work secured versus Construction revenue recognised that period (replenishment rate)
  • Backlog margin quality, not just size -- a bigger backlog at a thinner margin is not necessarily better

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Lendlease Group: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Lendlease Group: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

nav.title: NAV per share
nav.content:
NAV per share is the net asset value of the portfolio per share.

For Lendlease Group: the valuation compounds NAV and applies an exit discount; the share price discount to NAV is the second lever.

What to watch:

  • NAV total return
  • Discount to NAV versus history

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Lendlease Group: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Lendlease Group: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Lendlease Group: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Lendlease Group: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
